transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-10-07
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 mins
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (BlueRiver Head of Eng), Aisha Patel (BlueRiver FinOps), Ravi Shah (Platform Eng), Maya Lin (Security)

Summary (auto): Quick orientation on the Redwood Console usage analytics and per-route cost breakouts. Ran through sample routes, discussed KV cache/cacheing impact, and options for Dedicated capacity vs Hosted API for regulated PHI flows.

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. Uh, quick intros - i'm Liam, AE at Redwood, joining me is Priya who is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Priya: Hi folks, thanks, excited to show a quick walkthrough of the Console - we’ll focus on routes, per-route lenses, cost attribution and some knobs you can use to balance latency and spend.
[00:25] Carlos: Cool, quick note — we care about cost per inference and per-patient session, and also how to split this across product lines for reporting to our FinOps team.
[00:35] Aisha: Yeah, exactly. Our CFO wants a predictable monthly bill and alerts if any route goes off the rails.
[00:42] Liam: Totally, that's what the route mapping is for. Priya, can you share your screen?
[00:49] Priya: Yep, sharing now. Okay so this is the Console home. You'll see an overview—total tokens, latency P50/P95, and a cost pulse. We'll go into the Routes tab.
[01:10] Priya: (screen) Here are BlueRiver's example routes — intake:patient-summary, summarizer:clinical-notes, triage:initial-screen. Each route has its own dashboard. If you click the route you get a cost breakdown by model variant, and attribution to labels you define.
[01:29] Carlos: Nice, can we map these to our internal cost centers? Like product:telemedicine vs product:triage?
[01:36] Priya: Yes — route tagging supports arbitrary key:value tags. We can ingest tags via the API or map them in the Console UI. That mapping flows into the billing export and per-route reports.
[01:49] Aisha: How granular is the cost split? We need per-team and per-feature numbers, not just broad lumps.
[01:56] Priya: You can break down by route, model, and customer tag. There's also an attribution matrix for multi-route sessions — it uses heuristics to split tokens across contributing routes. It's configurable.
[02:12] Ravi: Quick technical q: how does KV cache impact cost? We saw big variance in our internal tests.
[02:18] Priya: Good question — KV cache reduces repeated decode cost for long chats. If you use prefix caching for similar contexts, tokens per request drop, so cost drops. In the Console you'll see hits/misses and the estimated token savings. Note: our runtime does K-V cache, sometimes transcribed as K V cash in older notes - sorry for the typo.
[02:36] Liam: Also note that batching changes unit cost. If you run in Dedicated capacity you can tune batch size and concurrency; the Console shows an 'effective tokens/sec' and the per-token cost estimate with current config.
[02:50] Carlos: About Dedicated vs Hosted — for PHI flows we likely need Private or Dedicated. What's the cost delta?
[02:56] Priya: Roughly, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower per-token at scale because the infra amortizes. Hosted is pay-as-you-go; per-token is slightly higher but zero infra ops. For private/VPC we add platform fee and support. I'll send a pricing sketch after.
[03:12] Aisha: For budgeting, will we get projected monthly spend if we input expected qps?
[03:18] Priya: Yes — under Forecasting you can simulate expected traffic by route. The forecast uses historical latency and batching characteristics. We also have a 'What if' tab to toggle quantization profiles and see cost changes.
[03:30] Liam: (interrupt) One caveat: quantization may affect output quality for some models; we recommend running a small eval deck. Priya will share our eval harness.
[03:40] Priya: I'll drop link to the eval harness and to the KV tuning guide in the follow-up.
[03:45] Carlos: Great. Can we look at an example breakdown by model family?
[03:50] Priya: Sure — on the route page choose 'Model breakdown'. See this chart: 70% usage on open-llm-3b quantized, 20% on open-llm-13b for long form, and 10% on an experimental Llama-2 variant. The Console shows token cost per model and the total. You can set fallback policies so if capacity for the 13b model is constrained, requests fall back to the 3b with a different prompt template.
[04:20] Aisha: How do we capture the quality delta when falling back? We need to know if user satisfaction drops.
[04:27] Priya: We attach a small set of eval prompts to the route and monitor quality metrics: rouge/embedding-similarity against a reference. If regression crosses threshold you'll get an alert. The Console ties regressions to recent configuration changes.
[04:40] Carlos: Do you have audit logs for token-level access? We need to show data lineage for compliance.
[04:46] Priya: Yes — audit trails include request hashes, route, model used, and time. For Private deployments we integrate with your KMS/HSM for key rotation records.
[04:55] Maya: On the security piece — we need SOC2 evidence plus SSO/SAML integration and RBAC scoping per route.
[05:02] Liam: We have a SOC2 package and an SSO integration guide. we'll schedule a security deep-dive with Maya.
[05:09] Maya: Ok, please send the SOC2 docs and the diagram of network flows for Private deployments.
[05:15] Liam: Will do.
[05:17] Priya: Back to Console, i'll show how to create an alert. You can set a threshold on 'cost-per-minute' or 'tokens-per-5min' per route. Alerts can fire to PagerDuty or slack channel. Here's a sample alert rule: route cost rises 20% day-over-day for 3 consecutive windows.
[05:35] Ravi: If we enable autoscaling, how do we avoid cost spikes?
[05:39] Priya: You can set max burst and a budget cap. Also, the Console supports a 'graceful degrade' policy: when spend exceeds threshold, it will route low-priority traffic to cheaper model variants or increase quantization.
[05:52] Carlos: Show me the billing export. We want to pull into our chargeback system.
[05:58] Priya: Sure — billing export is CSV/JSON, with per-request line items including route tags. You can push to an S3 bucket or call the billing API.
[06:12] Aisha: Any latency numbers on the cheaper variants? Our SLAs are P95 < 400ms for triage route.
[06:18] Priya: For triage (short context) the quantized 3b hits P95 ~220ms on Dedicated with small batch sizes. On Hosted it can be slightly higher depending on region. For long-context summarizer, P95 is higher — 600ms for 13b on worst-case. We'll share region-specific numbers.
[06:36] Carlos: I want to see an end-to-end demo of a request mapping to cost center.
[06:40] Priya: Ok watch this — sending a sample request to the API. You can see it land in the route activity stream, the tokens consumed, KV-cache hits shown, model chosen via routing, and the final cost assigned to the tag product:telemedicine/team:outreach. The Console shows the line item and you can export it.
[07:05] (short silence, screen demo continues)
[08:12] Priya: Note: sometimes transcription will show model names slightly off, like 'open LLM' vs 'open-llm', the export has canonical ids.
[08:20] Carlos: About pilot scope — we want to run 3 routes: intake, triage and summarizer on production traffic sampled at 10%. We want both Hosted and a Dedicated-config comparison.
[08:32] Liam: That makes sense. Our pilot SOW will propose the split and two-week benchmarking with traffic mirrored at 10% to Redwood.
[08:40] Aisha: What data retention options do we have for logs? We need to keep traces for 90 days but scrub PHI from payloads.
[08:48] Priya: You can configure retention policies per tenant and route. For PHI flows we recommend private deployment with in-transit encryption and request-level redaction rules. We'll share the data-flow diagram and redaction guidance.
[09:02] Ravi: Any limitations on request size for KV cache? We've got long clinical contexts.
[09:07] Priya: KV cache depends on model context window; larger windows increase mem usage on the host. We support continuous attention patterns and chunking; in the Console you can model memory usage for your traffic.
[09:20] (Various notes, team asks about SDKs)
[09:28] Liam: We have SDKs in Python/Node and an open sample app for BlueRiver's triage flow. I'll share repo link.
[09:35] Aisha: In terms of price transparency, will invoices include per-route breakdowns?
[09:39] Priya: Yes, invoices include aggregated per-route spend and the detailed export is available for internal chargeback.
[09:45] Carlos: Are there any gotchas with multi-region routing? We operate in NA and EU and need residency for some patients.
[09:53] Priya: You can pin certain routes to region via routing policy and enable fallback to nearest region while preserving residency constraints. The Console will show region-level usage and costs.
[10:05] (minutes pass — demonstration continues with charts and filtering)
[24:12] Priya: Quick note — the Optimize tab gives suggestions: increase batching for low-latency tolerant routes, enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, and try a quantized model variant for summarizer to save ~35% cost in our estimate.
[24:28] Aisha: Can Optimize run automatically? Like an auto-suggestion that modifies config?
[24:33] Priya: We support suggestions only; changes must be approved by an admin. For Dedicated we can also enable safelisted automated scaling policies.
[24:42] Carlos: Show me the audit trail for a config change.
[24:47] Priya: Here — change history includes user, timestamp, old/new values, and has links to the diff. You can lock routes to require 2FA or approvals for production changes.
[24:59] Maya: For the security deep-dive, we need the network diagram and the KMS integration examples. We'll want to review HSM support for key material.
[25:09] Liam: Noted. We'll attach those to the follow-up.
[25:12] Ravi: If we sign a Dedicated contract, how fast can you provision?
[25:17] Priya: Typical turnaround is 4-6 weeks depending on model footprint and region. We do capacity planning and can prioritize enterprise customers.
[25:26] Carlos: Pricing for Dedicated — is it fixed monthly seat or usage + baseline?
[25:31] Liam: It's a reserved capacity model: commit to a monthly GPU pool and you get lower per-token rates. We can model different commit levels in the proposal.
[25:39] Aisha: For the pilot, can we get a discounted trial for the Dedicated benchmarking?
[25:44] Liam: We usually run a pilot with trial credits for hosted and a short-term Dedicated bench offer — i'll include that in the SOW.
[25:52] (demo continues showing filtering by tag and date ranges)
[36:10] Priya: Here's a sample alert we set up earlier for BlueRiver sandbox: if tokens/day > 20k and cost/day > $2000, alert FinOps channel.
[36:22] Aisha: Perfect. Is there an API to silence alerts during deployments?
[36:27] Priya: Yes there's an alerts API — you can mute by tag, route or time window.
[36:34] Carlos: On the export side, can we sync to our data warehouse?
[36:38] Priya: We support push to S3, BigQuery, Snowflake via connector. We'll share the connector docs.
[36:45] Ravi: Do you surface inference-level embeddings so we can run our own analytics?
[36:50] Priya: We expose embeddings as a separate export; for PHI you can opt out of storing payloads.
[36:58] (discussion about contract terms briefly)
[40:12] Carlos: One last thing — can we set cost-based routing so certain high-cost requests are only allowed in off-peak or require approval?
[40:20] Priya: Yes, you can create policies that gate routes by budget windows or require manual approval. The Console shows a policy simulator so you can see impact before applying.
[40:32] Liam: Okay quick recap and next steps. We'll send the pilot SOW and pricing, Priya will share the benchmark runbook, and we'll schedule a security deep-dive.
[40:42] Aisha: Sounds good — thanks everyone.
[40:46] Carlos: Thanks all.
[40:48] (meeting wraps, small cross talk)

Notes on transcription: occasional errors on model names (llama vs llama2 vs Llama-2), and some product names were transcribed as 'Redwood Consolo' in the auto captions. Links referenced during the call: Pilot SOW draft (https://redwood.ai/pilot/BRH-draft), Eval harness (https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness), KV tuning guide (https://redwood.ai/docs/kv-tuning), Security pack (https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-pack).

End of transcript.
